items.stem: Define the term 'primary sector'.
items.answer: Businesses that extract natural resources, such as farming, fishing, forestry and mining.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – Businesses that extract natural resources, such as farming, fishing, forestry and mining. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why the tertiary sector usually grows as a country's economy develops.
items.answer: As incomes rise, people spend a larger share on services such as leisure, finance and health; manufacturing may move to lower-cost countries.
items.markingKey: 1 mark rising incomes/demand for services; 1 mark example; 1 mark manufacturing moving abroad or productivity changes. [3]

items.stem: Explain one problem for a country caused by deindustrialisation.
items.answer: Manufacturing jobs are lost, causing structural unemployment in regions where factories close, because workers lack the skills for service jobs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark problem; 1 mark explanation. [2]

items.stem: Petra Prints Ltd is a private limited company based in Amman, Jordan. It prints leaflets, posters and packaging for local businesses and employs about 35 people. A large customer has started to pay its invoices late. Explain how a decline in the primary sector in Jordan could affect Petra Prints.
items.answer: Points to develop for Petra Prints: the primary sector extracts raw materials; raw materials may have to be imported at higher cost; supply may be less reliable; lower incomes in rural areas may reduce demand.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: the primary sector extracts raw materials. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Petra Prints (printing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. raw materials may have to be imported at higher cost; supply may be less reliable. [3]

items.stem: Rising costs of imported packaging have cut its profit margins. Lagos Bites Ltd, a private limited company in Nigeria with about 700 employees, produces packaged snacks such as plantain chips and chin chin. Explain why Lagos Bites is classified in the sector it operates in, and how it depends on other sectors.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lagos Bites: businesses are classified by the main activity; it relies on suppliers in other sectors; it sells to customers in other sectors; all sectors are interdependent in the chain of production.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: businesses are classified by the main activity. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Lagos Bites (food processing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. it relies on suppliers in other sectors; it sells to customers in other sectors. [3]

items.stem: Lagos Bites Ltd is a private limited company based in Lagos, Nigeria. It produces packaged snacks such as plantain chips and chin chin and employs about 700 people. items.answer: For: new opportunities for service businesses; higher incomes increase demand; growth of knowledge-based industries. Against: manufacturers face decline and closure; structural unemployment; dependence on imported goods. Judgement: for Lagos Bites it depends mainly on the sector each business operates in, and also on the speed of change.

A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Lagos Bites. [10]

items.stem: Define the term 'public sector'.
items.answer: The part of the economy owned and controlled by the government, such as state-owned enterprises and public services.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The part of the economy owned and controlled by the government, such as state-owned enterprises and public services. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between a public limited company and a public sector organisation.
items.answer: A plc is in the private sector, owned by shareholders who can buy its shares on the stock exchange; a public sector organisation is owned and controlled by the government.
items.markingKey: 1 mark plc = private sector, shareholders; 1 mark public sector = government owned. [2]

items.stem: Explain two possible disadvantages of privatising a state-owned electricity company.
items.answer: Prices may rise as owners seek profit; and unprofitable services, such as supplying remote areas, may be cut.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark point, 1 mark explanation): higher prices, loss of social objectives, job losses, private monopoly. [4]

items.answer: Points to develop for Kaya Cycles: privatisation transfers a business to the private sector; the competitor may become more efficient and aggressive; prices in the market may fall; new investment may raise quality standards.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: privatisation transfers a business to the private sector. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Kaya Cycles (retail and repairs). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. the competitor may become more efficient and aggressive; prices in the market may fall. [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'sole trader'.
items.answer: A business owned by one person, who has unlimited liability.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – A business owned by one person, who has unlimited liability. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain the meaning and importance of limited liability.
items.answer: Shareholders can lose only the money they invested, not their personal possessions; this reduces their risk, so people are more willing to invest in companies.
items.markingKey: 1 mark meaning; 1 mark only investment at risk; 1 mark encourages investment/growth. [3]

items.stem: Explain two disadvantages for a sole trader of having unlimited liability.
items.answer: The owner's personal assets, such as their house, can be taken to pay business debts; and the risk discourages the owner from expanding or borrowing.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark point, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.answer: Points to develop for Savanna Fresh: growth needs more capital; limited liability reduces the owners' risk; more shareholders bring finance; a new structure affects control and disclosure.

items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'private limited company'?

The owners of a business are not personally liable for its debts; they can lose only the amount they invested.

items.stem: Explain two benefits to a franchisee of buying a franchise rather than starting an independent business.
items.answer: The franchisee uses an established brand that customers already trust, so sales are more likely; and it receives training and support from the franchisor, reducing the risk of failure.
